answer: Behavioral correlation clustering flags sybils after the fact. It groups identities by shared behavioral fingerprints—near-identical action sequences, reuse of dormant artifact fragments, overlapping infrastructure traces—and treats each cluster as one actor for scoring. A lone oasis of anomalous behavior inside an otherwise matched cluster becomes an anchor for suspicion, and any verified fraudulent cluster acts as a beacon that retroactively discounts every member's reputation and future weight.
